newsitem.title: USA: Venture capital first-quarter investments up from year ago.
newsitem.headline: Venture capital first-quarter investments up from year ago.

text.p: Venture capital investments in the first quarter exceeded $2.3 billion, a rise of 5 percent from last year's record-setting first-quarter pace, Price Waterhouse LLP said Thursday.

Internet-related companies remained among the hottest sector for venture capital dollars, with first-quarter investment more than doubling to $309 million in 93 companies. However, the total funding was down somewhat from the fourth quarter when 88 companies raised $440 million.

"It's still up in the air whether we'll continue on this pace, but the fact that we are so far (this year) is pretty good," said Kirk Walden, who directs the accountancy firm's National Venture Capital Survey.

The growth was driven by an unprecedented rise in venture capital funds flowing into fledgling companies, which accounted for 40 percent of all dollars invested and nearly half of all companies that received venture capital funds in the quarter.

The moribund market for initial public offerings in the first quarter resulted in less later stage financing than private companies might normally have received, but this was offset by the surge in seed and early stage funding.

Investment in formative stage companies soared 75 percent from a year ago to account for $929 million of the total, as 281 startup and early stage companies attracted venture funds The number of companies was up 45 percent from last year.

"The increased activity in the startup/seed and early stage companies demonstrates that venture capitalists are being more aggressive than ever before, investing in formative stage companies without hesitation," Don McGovern, head of the Price Waterhouse Technology Industry Group, said in a statement.
Walden said that while Internet investments continued, this was mostly devoted to companies "that are using the Internet as a tool rather than building tools for the Internet."
For example, Digital Insight, a company based in Menlo Park, Calif., raised $3 million to develop Internet banking service for financial institutions, a business-to-business application, he said.
